To find out how many years it will take for Carlos to start earning money on the lemon tree, we need to calculate his net profit per year and compare it to the initial cost of planting the tree.

**Step 1: Calculate the yearly revenue from selling lemons.**
Carlos gets 7 lemons each year and sells them for $1.50 each.
$\text{Yearly revenue} = 7 \times \$1.50 = \$10.50$

**Step 2: Calculate the yearly net profit.**
It costs $3 a year to water and feed the tree. Subtract this annual cost from the yearly revenue.
$\text{Yearly net profit} = \$10.50 - \$3.00 = \$7.50$

**Step 3: Calculate how many years it takes to break even.**
The initial cost to plant the tree is $90. Divide the initial cost by the yearly net profit to find out when he breaks even.
$\text{Years to break even} = \frac{\$90}{\$7.50} = 12 \text{ years}$

**Step 4: Determine when he starts earning money.**
At year 12, Carlos will have made exactly $90 in net profit ($7.50 \times 12 = $90), meaning he has broken even and his total profit is $0. To actually *start earning money* (have a total profit greater than $0), it will take one more year.
$12 + 1 = 13 \text{ years}$

Answer: 13
